claims: `GATE_TEST_FOCUS` still takes effect inside a real gate run started with `--no-lock` (`scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh:589-594`; the same false claim is in `docs/notes/agent-quality-gate-mechanics.md:1142-1146`): the refusal only checks `AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD`, which is not exported when the lock is disabled, so a focused run of 1 of 11 families exits 0, writes the success stamp, and the Trunk pre-push hook (`--skip-if-fresh`) reuses that stamp for up to 2 hours

The docs overstate the partition check (`docs/notes/agent-quality-gate-mechanics.md:1149-1153`): the check starts at `# >>> gate family body start`, so a test added in the prelude before `verify_gate_family_partition` runs in every focused mode and isn't caught; the doc's "a test line sits outside every family" is wrong
Nothing enforces the `arm_suite_abort_trap` first line: a future family that omits it loses the abort diagnostic silently
Nit: the solo runtimes in the table add up to about 696s, while the same doc says "~9-minute suite" and the gate says "measured at 525s alone"; either the table or the prose is stale

judge_reasoning.3829986398: The review never mentions output_file being unset when the abort trap fires under set -u. It calls ERR trap handling correct.
judge_reasoning.3829986403: The review says the partition check catches a line after the dispatch call. It never raises a second dispatch_gate_test_families call passing validation and running families twice.
judge_reasoning.3830003055: The review does not note that deleting the dispatch call still passes the partition check and silently exits 0.
judge_reasoning.3830042123: Review item 1 is this defect: GATE_TEST_FOCUS is honored under --no-lock (or AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK=0) because the guard only checks AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD, so a focused subset answers for the full gate.
judge_reasoning.3830042128: The review does not mention the hard-coded scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh path pin missing from the path-pin inventory.
judge_reasoning.3830695396: The review's doc findings cover the --no-lock claim, the partition scope and runtime totals. None addresses 'is set' versus 'is non-empty' or the 'reds the suite' wording.

1.why: The refusal at test.sh:600-605 checks only AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD and GITHUB_ACTIONS, and the gate exports LOCK_HELD only when it holds the lock (gate.sh:1143). This is the known item 'test.sh:628 Reject focus during lock-free gate runs'.

2.why: In the awk check, lines before '# >>> gate family body start' only update `previous` (the `body == 0` branch) and are never checked. A test line in the ~420-line prelude therefore passes, even though doc lines 1147-1149 say the check fails the suite on any test line outside every family. The code comment limits the check to marker-to-end; the doc drops that limit.

3.why: True that awk does not check for the arm_suite_abort_trap line, but all 11 run_*_family functions have it as their first line (grep count 11), and a missing call would only lose the abort diagnostic. This is a hypothetical future-maintenance concern, not a current defect.

4.why: The table does add up to 696s, but those are solo runtimes. run_gate caches output in gate_cache_dir, which is shared across families within one run and created fresh by mktemp each run, so a solo family starts cold. Solo times are expected to add up to more than the ~525s/~9-minute full run, so the numbers don't show that either one is stale.
